blueprint.title: Production Log Filter Daemon: Dual Misconfiguration
blueprint.scenario: A backend developer is chasing a silent data-quality bug in a log-processing pipeline. The system reads structured JSON application logs from /var/log/app/, runs them through a configurable filter daemon (/opt/logfilter/), and forwards 'clean' events to a downstream sink at /var/spool/filtered/. In production, the team is seeing two symptoms: (1) some known-malicious events are reaching the sink, and (2) some legitimate high-volume events are being dropped entirely. The daemon has ~1,200 lines across several modules—a config loader, a rule engine, a normalizer, and a dispatcher—and the symptoms only reproduce when the daemon processes realistic log traffic, not the tiny smoke-test fixture.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
The log filter daemon at /opt/logfilter/ is misbehaving in production. When run against the provided replay corpus at /var/log/app/replay/, it should:

1. Pass every event whose `severity` is `INFO` or lower (DEBUG, TRACE) through to /var/spool/filtered/ unchanged, regardless of any other field.
2. Reject every event where `severity` is ERROR or CRITICAL **and** the `source` field matches any pattern in /opt/logfilter/conf/blocklist.conf (one glob pattern per line).
3. For events with severity WARNING: pass through only if the `request_id` field is present and non-empty; drop silently otherwise.
4. Never drop or alter a field named `trace_id` in any event that reaches the sink.
5. Produce one JSON object per line in the sink files (newline-delimited JSON, no trailing commas, no arrays).

The daemon is invoked as: `python3 /opt/logfilter/main.py --config /opt/logfilter/conf/daemon.conf --input /var/log/app/replay/ --output /var/spool/filtered/`

After your fix, the verifier will run the daemon against a fresh hidden corpus of 2,000 events and check that every event is routed exactly according to the five rules above. The current code contains exactly two interacting configuration defects; fixing only one will cause the other's effect to surface on different event classes. Investigate by running the daemon on the replay corpus and observing which events are misrouted.
requirements: INFO/DEBUG/TRACE events always reach the sink, never dropped
ERROR/CRITICAL events matching any blocklist.conf glob are rejected; non-matching ones pass through
WARNING events with a present, non-empty request_id pass through; others are silently dropped
Any event that reaches the sink retains its trace_id field unchanged if it was present
Sink output is newline-delimited JSON (one object per line, no wrapping array)
Daemon exits 0 and processes all input files in the replay/corpus directory
environment: apt-get install -y python3-fnmatch (already in stdlib) — no extra apt needed
pip install: no external deps beyond stdlib
/opt/logfilter/ directory tree (~1,200 lines across): main.py, config_loader.py, rule_engine.py, normalizer.py, dispatcher.py, utils.py
/opt/logfilter/conf/daemon.conf: INI-style config; contains the two planted misconfigs as described below
/opt/logfilter/conf/blocklist.conf: ~40 glob patterns for malicious sources (e.g. 'crawler.*', 'bot-*', 'scraper_*', etc.)

/var/log/app/replay/: 6 JSON-log files, ~300 events total, covering all severity levels and source patterns, but only ~50 events exercise the interacting code path that reveals both bugs simultaneously

Bug 1 (config+data interaction, not visible by reading alone): daemon.conf sets severity_order = DEBUG,TRACE,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL but the rule_engine.py compares severities by list-index, and the config loader strips whitespace inconsistently—when a severity token has a leading space (e.g. ' WARNING'), the index lookup silently returns -1 (not found), causing WARNING to be treated as lower-than-DEBUG, so WARNING events pass even without request_id. This only surfaces on the ~80-event subset of the corpus that has WARNING severity—the smoke test has none.

Bug 2 (interacting with Bug 1): The normalizer.py applies a field-rename step driven by daemon.conf key field_aliases = trace_id:tid. This was meant to normalize an old field name on ingest, but the alias is applied bidirectionally—when writing to the sink, it renames trace_id back to tid, silently dropping the trace_id key from output. Bug 1 must be fixed first (correcting severity parsing); once WARNING events are correctly filtered, a second test class that checks trace_id preservation becomes non-trivially testable. If only Bug 2 is fixed, Bug 1 causes WARNING events to leak through without request_id, failing a different test class.

Plausible but uninvolved code: dispatcher.py has retry logic, batching, and file-rotation code (~300 lines) that is correct and irrelevant; normalizer.py has ~200 lines of timestamp normalization that works fine; utils.py has logging helpers
blueprint.internal_hint: Root cause 1 (observe_not_read): daemon.conf has severity_order with a leading space on ' WARNING' (and ' ERROR', ' CRITICAL'). The config_loader does `token.strip()` only when splitting on commas, but not after—actually it strips the first token and last but skips interior tokens due to a slice bug: `parts = line.split(','); return [parts[0].strip()] + parts[1:-1] + [parts[-1].strip()]`. So interior severity tokens retain their leading spaces. rule_engine.py does `self.severity_levels.index(event_severity)` and catches ValueError by returning -1, treating unknown severities as lower than DEBUG. The fix is correcting the config_loader's strip logic to apply `.strip()` to every token. This only shows up when running on WARNING/ERROR/CRITICAL events in volume—the smoke test has only INFO and DEBUG events. Root cause 2 (two_interacting_causes): normalizer.py reads field_aliases from daemon.conf and applies them in both directions (ingest rename AND output rename), renaming trace_id→tid in the output. The fix is making the alias map unidirectional (ingest only). After fixing Bug 1, the WARNING events that now correctly require request_id expose a new test class checking trace_id preservation on those events, revealing Bug 2. A solver who fixes only Bug 2 will see the hidden tests for WARNING-without-request_id still fail. A solver who fixes only Bug 1 will see trace_id preservation tests fail.
blueprint.trap: A naive agent runs the daemon on the smoke-test replay corpus, sees INFO/DEBUG events pass correctly and a few ERROR events from obvious bot sources get blocked, declares it working, and submits. The hidden corpus has 400 WARNING events (200 with request_id, 200 without), 300 ERROR/CRITICAL events from non-blocklisted sources, and 500 events with trace_id fields. The WARNING routing is wrong (both pass when they shouldn't, or both drop), and trace_id fields are silently renamed to tid in all output. A solver who fixes only the severity parsing will still fail the trace_id tests. A solver who only fixes trace_id aliasing will still fail the WARNING routing tests.
tests: Generate 200 WARNING events with request_id present: all must appear in sink output
Generate 200 WARNING events without request_id: none must appear in sink output
Generate 300 INFO/DEBUG/TRACE events: all must appear in sink output
Generate 150 ERROR events with source matching blocklist patterns: none must appear in sink
Generate 150 ERROR events with source NOT matching blocklist patterns: all must appear in sink
Generate 500 events with a trace_id field (mix of severities, all expected to pass): every event in sink must have trace_id key with original value (not renamed to tid or dropped)
Generate 50 CRITICAL events matching blocklist: all rejected; 50 CRITICAL not matching blocklist: all pass
Verify sink files contain valid newline-delimited JSON (parse each line independently, no array wrappers)
Verify daemon exits with code 0 when run on the hidden corpus directory

verifier_knob.name: corpus_size
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing corpus size and adding more edge cases (e.g. mixed-case severity strings, empty source fields, events with both trace_id and tid, glob patterns with wildcards in blocklist) raises difficulty. Lowering to 200 events with only canonical cases makes it easier.

expected_failure_modes: Agent reads the source code, spots the field_alias issue in normalizer.py (visible by reading), fixes only that, and misses the config parsing bug which only shows on WARNING-volume traffic
Agent runs the daemon on the replay corpus, sees most output looks correct (INFO/DEBUG dominate), doesn't probe the WARNING subset specifically, and misses both bugs

Agent fixes the severity_order parsing bug but doesn't notice the bidirectional alias application because the smoke test has no events with both a trace_id field and a severity that passes the fixed filter
Agent fixes both bugs but introduces a new bug in the config_loader strip logic that breaks CRITICAL severity parsing, causing non-blocklisted CRITICAL events to be dropped

Agent patches normalizer.py to not rename trace_id on output but leaves the config-loader bug, so WARNING events are still misrouted; tests that check WARNING+trace_id together catch both failure modes at once but agent thinks only one fix was needed

speedrun: # Identify bug 1: parts[1:-1] not stripped in config_loader.py
# Identify bug 2: bidirectional alias rename in normalizer.py
sed -i 's/\[parts\[0\]\.strip()\] + parts\[1:-1\] + \[parts\[-1\]\.strip()\]/[p.strip() for p in parts]/' /opt/logfilter/config_loader.py
# Edit normalizer.py to remove output-direction alias application (use editor or sed)
python3 -I -c "import json,os; [json.loads(l) for fn in os.listdir('/var/spool/filtered/') for l in open('/var/spool/filtered/'+fn) if l.strip()]"
invalid_failure_risks: Bug 1 is described as 'observe_not_read' but the slice defect in config_loader.py is fully visible by static code reading — a careful agent who reads all source files will find it without running any traffic, undermining the intended difficulty lever.

The replay corpus has only ~80 WARNING events but the task says symptoms 'only reproduce on realistic log traffic, not tiny smoke-test fixture' — if the replay corpus is large enough to show the bug, a careful agent running it once may spot misrouted events directly without needing to understand the root cause.

The fix for Bug 1 via sed or string replacement is fragile — the exact whitespace in daemon.conf must match what config_loader.py expects; if the builder uses slightly different quoting or escaping, the fix may not apply cleanly.

The verifier description says 'adversarial corpus' but the test cases are fully specified in the blueprint (exact counts: 200 WARNING with request_id, 200 without, etc.) — there is no adversarial element beyond the stated rules, making this a standard functional test.

The interaction between Bug 1 and Bug 2 described ('fixing Bug 1 reveals Bug 2') is slightly overstated — Bug 2 (bidirectional alias) affects ALL events reaching the sink regardless of severity, so it is independently testable even before Bug 1 is fixed, just on INFO/DEBUG events with trace_id fields.
If the smoke-test replay corpus includes any events with trace_id fields at INFO/DEBUG severity, Bug 2 is detectable even without fixing Bug 1, weakening the 'interacting bugs' claim.
review.reasons: The task's central difficulty claim — that Bug 1 only surfaces on runtime data and cannot be found by reading — is false; the slice bug in config_loader.py (`parts[1:-1]` not stripped) is statically visible in ~10 lines of code, making this solvable in ~20 commands by a careful code reader. Additionally, Bug 2 (bidirectional alias) affects all severities reaching the sink, so it is independently discoverable on INFO/DEBUG events with trace_id before Bug 1 is fixed, breaking the claimed 'interacting causes' structure. The genuine_difficulty score of 2 disqualifies acceptance under the scoring rules (average cannot reach 3.6 with a 2 in one category when others are capped by this flaw).
fixes: To make Bug 1 truly 'observe_not_read': instead of a visible slice bug in config_loader.py, embed the misconfiguration purely in daemon.conf (e.g., severity_order uses a Unicode non-breaking space character before WARNING that looks identical to a regular space in most editors), so the code is correct but the config data is subtly wrong — this cannot be found by reading code alone.

To strengthen the interacting-bugs structure: make Bug 2 conditional on severity level (e.g., the alias is only applied when the severity index exceeds a threshold set in daemon.conf), so Bug 2 literally cannot manifest until Bug 1's severity parsing is corrected — this enforces true sequencing.

Reduce the replay corpus WARNING event count to 0 (smoke test has only INFO/DEBUG/ERROR) so running the daemon on replay produces no evidence of Bug 1; only running against volume traffic (or the hidden corpus) reveals it.
Add a third 'distractor' config key in daemon.conf that looks suspicious but is actually correct, to slow agents who pattern-match on 'anything unusual in the config must be a bug'.

Specify that the verifier checks trace_id preservation ONLY on WARNING events that correctly passed (not INFO/DEBUG), so Bug 2 is undetectable until Bug 1 is fixed — this enforces strict sequencing and validates the 'two interacting causes' claim.
